title: Applied ML & Evals: Centralized Playbooks (Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Onboarding, Guardrails, Quantization, Regression)
author: Jordan Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This document centralizes Redwood's applied-ML and evaluation playbooks. It covers the eval harness onboarding flow, prompt set and benchmark curation, model onboarding checklist, quality guardrails, quantization profile guidance, and a reproducible regression triage process. Use this as the canonical reference for cross-team collaboration between Applied ML, Serving Runtime, Platform, and SRE.

Scope
-----
Applies to: model engineers, applied-ML engineers, evaluation owners, runtime integration engineers, and on-call SREs.

Goals
-----
- Ensure consistent, reproducible model evaluation and onboarding across hosted/dedicated/private deployments.
- Minimize production regressions with automated evals and clear triage steps.
- Provide standardized quantization profiles and safety/quality guardrails.

Ownership and Contacts
----------------------
- Primary owner: Applied ML team (applied-ml@redwood.com)
- Runtime integration: eng-serving-runtime (runtime-infra@redwood.com)
- Observability & Dashboards: eng-platform (platform-observability@redwood.com)
- Escalation: oncall SRE (see oncall roster in /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response)

Key Services and Dashboards
---------------------------
- eval-harness (service): orchestrates batch and streaming eval runs.
- evaluator-service: microservice for metric computation and example-level traces.
- applied-ml-evals-dashboard: Grafana board with per-prompt/per-model metrics.
- regression-triage-tracker: Jira board for regression incidents.

SLOs and Thresholds (applied eval infra)
----------------------------------------
| Metric | Target | Alert threshold | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Eval job completion (48h end-to-end) | 99% | <98% | Applied ML infra |
| Example-level metric compute latency | <3s per example | any >5s p95 | evaluator-service |
| Regression detection (automated) | 100% coverage for critical prompt sets | miss critical >0 | Applied ML |

Eval Harness Onboarding (quickstart)
-----------------------------------
1. Request access: open a request to applied-ml-evals access group with your service account.
2. Create an eval config: follow the eval config schema in examples below.
3. Run locally: use the eval-harness CLI to validate (see examples).
4. Submit for CI: create a PR against evaluations repo with your config and sample golden outputs.
5. Add to dashboard: request a dashboard panel via platform-observability.

Eval Config Example (YAML)
-------------------------
```yaml
name: customer-support-qa-regression
model: redwood/llama-13b-v2
prompt_set: cs-qa-2026-03
metrics:
  - exact_match
  - f1
  - rouge_l
  - calibrated_entropy
batching:
  max_tokens: 2048
  batch_size: 16
quantization_profile: int8-default
environment:
  runtime: redwood-runtime:prod
  region: us-west1
```

Prompt Sets and Benchmarks: Curation Guidelines
------------------------------------------------
- Ownership: each prompt set must have an owner and a documented acceptance criteria.
- Composition: each set should include:
  - 200+ examples for model-quality evaluations; 50-100 examples for smoke/CI sets.
  - clear labels for expected output type (string, JSON-schema, classification).
  - edge-case examples with annotations for failure modes.
- Metadata: include tags (customer, vertical, safety, production), date collected, and source.
- Versioning: use semantic versioning for prompt sets (e.g., cs-qa-2026-03 v1.2).

Benchmarking Best Practices
--------------------------
- Run full benchmarks nightly for gold models; run smoke sets on every PR.
- Use evaluator-service to produce per-example traces and store them in S3 with consistent keys: s3://redwood-evals/{model}/{prompt_set}/{date}/.
- Store metric thresholds adjacent to prompt set metadata.

Model Onboarding Checklist (must complete before production rollout)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Model card created and reviewed (fields: architecture, training_corpora, known_biases, recommended_quantization_profiles).
2. Eval harness configs added for: smoke, nightly, and canary evaluation sets.
3. Performance benchmarks recorded: latency p50/p95, throughput, memory usage under typical load.
4. Quantization profile validated for target hardware (see table below).
5. Security scan (dependency checks) completed.
6. Release cadence and rollback plan documented.
7. Owner and secondary on-call assigned.

Quantization Profiles (recommended defaults)
-------------------------------------------
| Profile name | Description | Recommended hardware | Expected token p95 overhead | Notes |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| float16-default | Baseline fp16 for highest fidelity | A100/P4d | 1.0x | Default for new models unless memory constrained |
| int8-default | 8-bit weight quantization (symmetric) | T4/GPU-streaming / GR8 | 0.75x | Good cost/latency tradeoff; validate quality on prompt sets |
| int4-aggressive | 4-bit quantization for research/low-cost | NVL-series | 0.6x | Use only after regression tests pass; expect decreased fidelity on some tasks |

Quantization Validation Steps
-----------------------------
1. Run full eval suite on float16 baseline and target quantized profile.
2. Compare core metrics: exact_match, f1, bleu/rouge where applicable.
3. Flag any metric regression > 2% absolute for manual triage.
4. Run curated adversarial prompt subset (10% of prompt set) to detect distributional failure.

Quality Guardrails and Safety Checks
-----------------------------------
- Automatic filters: profanity filter, personal-identifiable-info (PII) redaction detector, hallucination heuristics.
- Output schema enforcement: JSON schema validation for structured outputs. Failures route to the evaluator-service and are surfaced in the dashboard.
- Canary rollout policy: start with 1% traffic, run canary prompt sets for 24h, check regressions, then incrementally increase (1%, 5%, 20%, 50%, 100%).

Regression Triage Playbook (incident response for eval regressions)
------------------------------------------------------------------
Trigger: automated alert from applied-ml-evals-dashboard when a critical prompt set metric crosses threshold.
Immediate steps (within 30 min):
1. Acknowledge alert and create an incident in regression-triage-tracker.
2. Capture context: model version, quantization profile, runtime revision, recent infra changes (CI/CD), and sample failed examples (from evaluator-service).
3. Rollback decision: if user-facing SLA impacted or metric delta >5% absolute on critical set, follow rollback policy in Model Onboarding Checklist.
4. Triage owner responsibilities:
   - Reproduce locally using eval-harness with the flagged prompt set and same runtime config.
   - Run binary search across recent model revisions and quantization profiles to identify regression introduction point.
5. If regression is due to model quality: open a model-regression ticket assigned to model-owner.
6. If regression is due to runtime or kernel change: escalate to eng-serving-runtime and include profiler traces.
7. Document root cause and postmortem within 72 hours if production impact > 1 hour.

Postmortem and Retro
--------------------
- Postmortem owner is the triage owner. Required sections: timeline, impact, root cause, contributing factors, action items (with owners and due dates).
- Schedule a retro with Applied ML, Runtime, SRE, and Product for high-impact regressions.

CI/CD Integration
----------------
- Smoke evals must run on every merge to main for eval configs and prompt-set changes.
- Nightly runs produce stable artifacts in S3 and a JSON summary (schema below).

Nightly summary example (JSON payload as string stored alongside artifacts):
{"model":"redwood/llama-13b-v2","prompt_set":"cs-qa-2026-03","date":"2026-11-15","metrics":"{\"exact_match\":0.842,\"f1\":0.79}","artifact_path":"s3://redwood-evals/redwood-llama-13b-v2/cs-qa-2026-03/2026-11-15/"}

Access and Governance
---------------------
- Prompt sets with customer-sensitive content must be marked confidentiality:restricted and require Product and Legal approval before inclusion in nightly/regression detection.
- Model cards and eval results are retained for 3 years by default; exceptions require Security sign-off.

Appendix: Useful CLI snippets
----------------------------
Validate config locally:
$ eval-harness validate --config ./configs/cs-qa-eval.yaml
Run a smoke eval:
$ eval-harness run --config ./configs/cs-qa-eval.yaml --profile smoke --output ./runs/local-run-$(date +%F).json
Submit nightly job (internal Jenkins):
$ jenkins-cli build evals-nightly -p MODEL=redwood/llama-13b-v2 -p PROMPT_SET=cs-qa-2026-03

Frequently Asked Questions
--------------------------
Q: When do I use int8 vs int4 profiles?
A: Start with int8-default for production cost savings. Only consider int4-aggressive after passing full regression triage and when token-cost savings justify the risk.

Q: Who approves prompt sets with customer data?
A: Product + Legal must sign off; add the prompt set to the related_pages list and set confidentiality:restricted.
